# data-nosnippet

*Directive*

An HTML attribute that keeps a marked part of a page out of Google's snippets.

**Glossary** (*nosnippet and data-nosnippet*): nosnippet stops text snippets and video previews for a page and keeps its content out of AI Overviews and AI Mode as a direct input; the data-nosnippet attribute hides only a marked part of the page.

Narrative: the topic [Snippets and preview controls](../topics/snippet-controls.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

7 claims mention it: 1 from Google's documentation, 4 shown or said at the event (2 confirmed by Google docs, 2 consistent with Google docs), 2 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Control your snippets in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag).

- [`D2-C079`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Docs: Google's robots meta tag specification says data-nosnippet may be extracted both before and after rendering, so the attribute should not be added to or removed from existing elements with JavaScript. `[D2-C079, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C077`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The data-nosnippet attribute can be used on only a handful of HTML elements. `[D2-C077, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C078`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Broken HTML can widen data-nosnippet: if a div marked data-nosnippet is not closed properly, the rest of the page can be blocked from the snippet as well. `[D2-C078, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C076`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller said data-nosnippet is rarely needed but lets a site keep a specific piece of text, such as a business phone number, out of the snippet, so the page can still be found for it while searchers have to visit the page to see it. `[D2-C076, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C080`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: John Mueller said valid HTML is technically not a ranking factor but does matter for controls such as data-nosnippet. `[D2-C080, stage, John Mueller, Day 2]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D2-C081`](../sessions/D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) Analysis: To hide one detail, such as a phone number, a price or a direct answer, instead of the whole snippet, wrap it in data-nosnippet on a span, div or section in the server HTML and validate the HTML so that an unclosed element cannot hide the rest of the page from snippets. `[D2-C081, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`
- [`D2-C731`](../sessions/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) Analysis: Treat nosnippet, data-nosnippet and max-snippet as AI visibility settings too: Google lists them as the controls for content in AI features, and if AI answers are built from index snippets, as Google said on stage, a blocked or shortened snippet leaves AI Overviews and AI Mode less to use. `[D2-C731, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-HTM-05` **SHOULD** · Documented: Write valid HTML and close every element (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-IDX-07` **MAY** · Documented: Use data-nosnippet on a span, div or section to keep one detail out of snippets (6 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
